{"parentUuid":"4e6991bc-20da-4a1b-8aec-7c20a6ad8964","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["plugin:context7:context7","plugin:serena:serena"],"addedBlocks":["## plugin:context7:context7\nUse this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. {"parentUuid":"6ff7f7fd-374b-4f85-92b5-ddb0ffd16edc","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- empirical-probe-first: Probe ALL viable strategies in a multi-option ladder BEFORE committing to one. Use when a session-plan / decision-ADR / spec presents ≥3 strategy options (e.g. \"Strategy A1/A2/A3\" or \"alternative B/C/D\") and the recommended option's source-evidence may be stale. Outputs a probe matrix per strategy + commit decision with empirical citation. Pairs with `vendor-api-probe.sh` (deterministic detection layer; SessionStart hook) and `decompose-work` (deterministic-vs-LLM split per probe). Charter promotion target — codifies L-S32-1 doctrine surfaced at S32 Track A pivot (master-plan recommended A2 vnstock alternate; empirical probe rejected A1+A2; A3 SSI direct httpx adopted instead).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. To be codified in `proposals/decision-discipline.md` § Promotion target priority during S16 IMPL.\n\n### Q-E4 — Auto-Detected-Drift Recovery Flow\n\n- **fire_when**: S5 Track 7 (`autonomous-protocol.md` recovery section) OR S8 Track 9 (paired with E1) → fired S15 PLAN 2026-04-29\n- **status**: closed\n- **fired_at**: 2026-04-29 (S15 PLAN Batch 3)\n- **closed_at**: 2026-04-29 (S15 PLAN Batch 3, same turn)\n- **source**: bundle 002 cluster E\n- **question**: If drift auto-detected mid-session, recovery flow?\n- **options**: A: HALT immediately; emit ALERT; require human resume / B: HALT only if charter-tier; SOFT-WARN otherwise / C: Open Q&A bundle with detected drift + 3 remediation options; let human pick async / D: Auto-revert to last clean checkpoint + emit notification / E: open answer\n- **answer**: C (Recommended) — Open Q&A bundle with detected drift + 3 remediation options; let human pick async. Matches UP-06 NO-Silent-Default + mobile-remote use case. To be codified in `proposals/autonomous-protocol.md` § Drift recovery flow during S16 IMPL.\n\n### Q-2.1 — Skill-Tool Autonomous Mode Policy\n\n- **fire_when**: S5 Track 7 `autonomous-protocol.md` authoring → fired S15 PLAN 2026-04-29\n- **status**: closed\n- **fired_at**: 2026-04-29 (S15 PLAN Batch 2)\n- **closed_at**: 2026-04-29 (S15 PLAN Batch 2, same turn)\n- **source**: `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/2026-04-29-003-up05-askuser-permissions-rawsessions.md` cluster Q2\n- **question**: For autonomous run, how to handle Skill tool prompts (Anthropic-designed always-prompt)?\n- **options**: A: Avoid Skill calls in autonomous mode (replace with inline procedures + agent dispatch) / B: Skill calls only in SUPERVISED mode; gate autonomous loops to NOT call skills / C: Batch Skill calls at session-start under explicit user approval (one-time per session) / D: Accept friction — pause on Skill prompt; not deal-breaker / E: open answer\n- **answer**: B (Recommended) — Skill calls only in SUPERVISED mode; gate autonomous loops to NOT call skills (replace with inline procedures or subagent dispatch). Everything here represents **agent state, decisions, plans, observations, learning**. Agents WRITE here freely (within constitution rules); humans READ here but normally do not edit.\n\nThis separation exists to prevent two failure modes from orch:\n1. **Charter drift via shared-workspace mutation** (orch CF-DOGFOOD-2)\n2. **Human cognitive overload from dense session logs** (UP02 §1.3 — \"human đối mặt hàng chục spec/document quá tải nếu không sắp xếp khoa học\")\n\nThe agent owns this directory but must keep it AUDITABLE — every artifact provenance-linked, every decision sourced.\n\n---\n\n## Subdirectories\n\n| Path | Purpose | Lifecycle |\n|---|---|---|\n| `constitution/` | **IMMUTABLE without explicit user approval**. Charter-tier rules (autonomous-protocol, model-routing, identity-scope, etc.). Track 7 produces drafts in `proposals/`; user explicit approve to move here. | Edit denied by .claude/settings.json; Write only via human approval gate |\n| `memory/project.md` | High-level project state; phase tracker; ADRs (last 5). Update on phase boundaries + architectural decisions. | Long-lived; trim to most recent decisions |\n| `memory/current-execution.md` | **THE single routing source of truth**. Active phase + active session + autonomous_mode flag + routing table. Read FIRST every session. | Long-lived; updated each session boundary |\n| `memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules from real experience (post-mortem / drift / user correction). Append-only mostly. | Long-lived |\n| `memory/decisions/` | Sequential ADRs (`NNN-<slug>.md`) + `_template.md` + `README.md` index. 12-field schema (Track 2). | Append-only; supersession via status field |\n| `memory/sessions/` | One file per session: `YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`. What happened, decisions made, files touched. | Append-only |\n| `memory/observations/` | Subagent return artifacts (per Track 6 spec). Each subagent writes one observation file describing what it did. | Append; cleaned periodically by aggregator |\n| `memory/checkpoints/` | Session handoff state for self-reboot (Track 5). `latest.md` is canonical pointer; timestamped historical files retained. | Append + latest.md updated each checkpoint |\n| `memory/patterns-discovered/` | Pattern mining outputs (Track 0 — DONE) + ongoing pattern catalog. | Append; significant patterns promoted to constitution |\n| `memory/drift-logs/` | Drift-check (DR1-DR12) results; runs on hook + on-demand. | Time-series append |\n| `memory/post-mortems/` | After significant failure or thesis-revoked event: what failed, root cause, prevention rule. | Append |\n| `memory/thesis-log/` | Stock-domain thesis exploration entries. Read-only for IMPL sessions. | Append + revisited per calibration |\n| `memory/sync-tracker/` | Track 8a output: Confidence Score SQLite + weights.yaml + auto-rendered `_index.md`. | Live updated by hooks |\n| `memory/self-awareness/` | Track 9 output: model × effort × thinking profile cards + known-issues + best-practices. | Live updated by Stop-hook aggregator |\n| `memory/mistake-log.md` | Track 7 deliverable: structured failure catalog. What went wrong / Root cause / Prevention rule / Severity. | Append; pre-flight read by all agents |\n| `session-plans/pending/` | Plans authored, awaiting execution. Phase 0 plan lives here. | Move to `completed/` when done |\n| `session-plans/completed/` | Executed plans; archived for reference + retrospective input. | Append |\n| `quality-reports/{deterministic,probabilistic,drift-reports}/` | Tier-1/2/3 gate outputs (CLAUDE.md § Quality Gates). | Per-run files |\n| `ubiquitous-language/` | DDD glossary + domain-mapping + drift-log. Stockforge stock-domain vocabulary. | Append; canonical via `/drill-me` |\n| `calibration/` | Empirical hit-rate data per signal type. Confidence claims MUST trace here (CLAUDE.md hard rule). | Append per thesis post-mortem |\n| `research/` | Research notes from `research-scanner` subagent dispatches (e.g., reference-repo studies). | Append |\n\n---\n\n## Contract Rules (BINDING)\n\n1. **Constitution is immutable absent explicit human approval.** `Edit/Write` to `agent-workspace/constitution/**` is in `.claude/settings.json` deny list. Track 7 writes constitution drafts to `proposals/`; user explicit approve moves them.\n\n2. **`memory/decisions/` is append-mostly + supersession-status.** Don't delete decisions; mark `status: superseded-by-D-NNN` to revoke. Sequential numbering (`001`, `002`, ...) — don't reuse numbers.\n\n3. **`current-execution.md` is the routing source-of-truth.** No skill, agent, or command may hardcode phase paths or session paths from memory; resolve via this file. Stale paths in CLAUDE.md or skills = anti-pattern.\n\n4. **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`.** Immutable. Vault writes only to `wiki/`. (Established in stockforge CLAUDE.md.)\n\n5. **Provenance is mandatory.** Every decision file references its source (human prompt / spec clause / drift detection / agent inference). Every thesis cites source + as-of date (I-S2). Every confidence claim cites historical hit rate (I-S20-equivalent).\n\n6. **Agents never `git commit` in this directory unless user explicitly requests.** Stage only.\n\n7. **`patterns-discovered/` artifacts are READ-ONLY for production code.** Patterns must be promoted to constitution / skills / hook scripts before becoming binding. (Otherwise they're informal notes, not contracts.)\n\n---\n\n## Reading Priority for Agent\n\nPer `agent-workspace/constitution/autonomous-protocol.md` (Track 7) and stockforge `CLAUDE.md` § Session Protocol:\n\n1. **`memory/current-execution.md`** — first; resolve active track\n2. **`memory/project.md`** — project state\n3. **`memory/checkpoints/latest.md`** if a recent checkpoint exists (within last 24h) — resume context\n4. **`memory/agent-notes.md`** — learned rules\n5. **`memory/mistake-log.md`** — pre-flight failure catalog\n6. **Last 3 files in `memory/sessions/`** — recent context\n7. **`session-plans/pending/<active-plan>.md`** — current plan\n8. **Relevant constitution files** as task demands (don't load all every session)\n9. **Relevant skills + agents + commands** as task demands\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns to Avoid\n\n(From `memory/patterns-discovered/SYNTHESIS.md` § 6, full catalog 23 items. Highest-priority for this directory:)\n\n- **AP-1 Same-agent self-review** — never review your own implementation; dispatch fresh-context verifier\n- **AP-2 Self-track wind-down** — `.transcript-tokens` real-transcript is authoritative, not LLM self-track\n- **AP-5 Charter-coherence defer overriding user-CRITICAL** — re-read all `user_prompt/*` at every phase entry; never silently defer USER-CRITICAL\n- **AP-7 Performative SC ticking** — defer with explicit prerequisites > fire vacuous proposals\n- **AP-8 Pre-staged work causing checkpoint drift** — update `current-execution.md` immediately on task complete, not session-end\n- **AP-17 Identity drift** — stockforge is AI-first VN stock advisory; not generic financial framework (see `constitution/identity-scope.md` once Track 7 ships)\n- **AP-23 Continuous LLM-Guardian** — deterministic hooks = Guardian; LLM Guardian only at session-end aggregation\n\n---\n\n## Connection to human-workspace/\n\nThis directory is the agent's domain. Human's domain is `human-workspace/`. The two communicate through:\n- Human → Agent: `human-workspace/user_prompt/`, `human-workspace/decisions/`\n- Agent → Human: `human-workspace/notifications/`, `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/`\n- Bidirectional: `human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/` — agent writes pending; either human or agent (per Auto-mv rule below) moves resolved bundles to answered/\n- Audit trail: this directory's `memory/decisions/` references `human-workspace/` source files via path pointers\n\n**Auto-mv rule (HH-E.2 — D-031 ratification, 2026-05-05)**: Agent MAY mv a bundle from `q-and-a/pending/` to `q-and-a/answered/` IFF ALL of the following hold:\n\n1. **Frontmatter signal**: bundle frontmatter `status:` field value starts with one of: `answered-`, `closed-`, `resolved-`. Examples already in repo: `answered-via-chat`, `answered-via-AskUserQuestion`, `answered-2026-05-04-via-chat`. Detection is deterministic (head -20 of file + grep `^status:`).\n2. **No human-veto signal**: bundle frontmatter has NO `wait_until:` ISO-8601 timestamp greater than current epoch — if present, agent MUST defer mv until that timestamp passes. Allows human to override auto-mv per-bundle without contract amendment.\n3. **No global pause**: file `human-workspace/q-and-a/.auto-mv-paused` does NOT exist — global kill switch for the auto-mv mechanism (single empty file presence pauses all auto-mv).\n4. **Hook validation**: the mv is performed by `scripts/hooks/qa-pending-auto-mover.sh` (Stop hook). Direct manual `mv` invocation by agent (e.g. via Bash tool) is STILL forbidden — only the validated hook path is authorized.\n\nAgent never writes to `human-workspace/` outside the designated `q-and-a/pending/` write channel + the auto-mv rule above + `notifications/` write channel (existing).\n","contentDiffersFromDisk":false},"displayPath":"agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"9fbad7cf-1bdd-4a3c-bb63-f36c3eb96f29","timestamp":"2026-05-06T07:15:12.139Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"764a01ea-a879-4d2c-840d-5087aa25d2e4","version":"2.1.124","gitBranch":"main"}

L-S10-1: if/then/fi only; split-local.\n17\tset -uo pipefail\n18\ttrap 'exit 0' ERR\n19\t\n20\tPROJECT_DIR=\"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}\"\n21\tHOOKS_DIR=\"$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/hooks\"\n22\tLOG=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log\"\n23\tNOTIF_DIR=\"$PROJECT_DIR/human-workspace/notifications\"\n24\tTS=\"$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)\"\n25\t\n26\tmkdir -p \"$(dirname \"$LOG\")\" 2>/dev/null || true\n27\t\n28\tVIOLATIONS=0\n29\tVIOLATION_LIST=\"\"\n30\t\n31\temit() {\n32\t  local code=\"$1\" file=\"$2\" detail=\"$3\"\n33\t  VIOLATIONS=$(( VIOLATIONS + 1 ))\n34\t  VIOLATION_LIST=\"${VIOLATION_LIST}  - ${code}: ${file} — ${detail}\"$'\\n'\n35\t}\n36\t\n37\t# === Check 1: L-S11-1 Phase 0 portability — no python/jq/yq/pip/npm in scripts/hooks ===\n38\t# Exempt: comments, strings, and explicit Phase-1+ stubs marked with \"# PHASE-1+\" guard comment.\n39\tif [ -d \"$HOOKS_DIR\" ]; then\n40\t  for f in \"$HOOKS_DIR\"/*.sh; do\n41\t    [ ! -f \"$f\" ] && continue\n42\t    bn=\"$(basename \"$f\")\"\n43\t    # Skip self.\n44\t    [ \"$bn\" = \"bash-hook-lint.sh\" ] && continue\n45\t    # Strip comments + heredocs roughly: scan only \"executable\" lines (not # comments).\n46\t    NON_COMMENT=\"$(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n47\t    # Look for forbidden tooling invocations as command tokens.\n48\t    if printf '%s' \"$NON_COMMENT\" | grep -qE '(^|[[:space:]`(|&;])(python3?|jq|yq|pip|pip3|npm|pnpm)([[:space:]]|$)'; then\n49\t      emit \"L-S11-1-PORTABILITY\" \"$bn\" \"non-Phase-0-portable invocation (python/jq/yq/pip/npm) — Phase 0 doctrine = bash + POSIX only\"\n50\t    fi\n51\t  done\n52\tfi\n53\t\n54\t# === Check 4: L-S43b-9 printf format-string starting with `-` needs `--` sentinel ===\n55\t# `printf '-foo'` interprets `-foo` as an option flag, not as the format string. Fix is\n56\t# `printf -- '-foo'`. Encountered 2x during HR-3 deploy per L-S43b-9. False-positive-safe:\n57\t# matches only lines where printf is followed by a literal quoted dash, AND the same line\n58\t# does NOT also contain `printf --` (which means the sentinel is already present).\n59\tif [ -d \"$HOOKS_DIR\" ]; then\n60\t  for f in \"$HOOKS_DIR\"/*.sh; do\n61\t    [ ! -f \"$f\" ] && continue\n62\t    bn=\"$(basename \"$f\")\"\n63\t    [ \"$bn\" = \"bash-hook-lint.sh\" ] && continue\n64\t    BAD=\"$(grep -nE \"printf[[:space:]]+['\\\"]-\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null | grep -vE \"printf[[:space:]]+--\" || true)\"\n65\t    if [ -n \"$BAD\" ]; then\n66\t      emit \"L-S43b-9-PRINTF-DASH\" \"$bn\" \"printf format starts with '-' without '--' sentinel — use 'printf -- ...'\"\n67\t    fi\n68\t  done\n69\tfi\n70\t\n71\t# === Check 2: L-S13-1 producer-consumer log path mismatch (silent telemetry brick) ===\n72\t# Heuristic: declared LOG-like variable but never used as redirect target within same file.\n73\tif [ -d \"$HOOKS_DIR\" ]; then\n74\t  for f in \"$HOOKS_DIR\"/*.sh; do\n75\t    [ ! -f \"$f\" ] && continue\n76\t    bn=\"$(basename \"$f\")\"\n77\t    [ \"$bn\" = \"bash-hook-lint.sh\" ] && continue\n78\t    # Extract variable names matching *LOG*|*FILE*|*OUTPUT*|*PATH* pattern that get assigned a path-looking value.\n79\t    DECL_VARS=\"$(grep -oE '^[A-Z_]+(LOG|FILE|OUTPUT|PATH|DIR)[A-Z_]*=' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/=$//' | sort -u || true)\"\n80\t    for v in $DECL_VARS; do\n81\t      [ -z \"$v\" ] && continue\n82\t      # Skip universally-known env vars that are inputs not outputs.\n83\t      case \"$v\" in\n84\t        PROJECT_DIR|HOOKS_DIR|CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR|HOOK_LOG|LOOP_DIR|DOGFOOD_DIR|NOTIF_DIR|EVENTS_DIR|INDEX_DIR|ARCHIVE_DIR) continue ;;\n85\t      esac\n86\t      # Check for \"$VAR\" or ${VAR} appearing on right side of >> or > redirect, OR as `tee $VAR`.\n87\t      if ! grep -qE \"(>>?|tee[[:space:]]+(-a[[:space:]]+)?)[[:space:]]*[\\\"]?\\\\\\$\\\\{?${v}\\\\}?\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null; then\n88\t        # Also accept if VAR is read FROM, or is a path argument to common command (find/cd/test/ls/mkdir/cp/mv/echo/printf/...)\n89\t        if ! grep -qE \"[\\\"]?\\\\\\$\\\\{?${v}\\\\}?\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null | grep -qvE \"^[A-Z_]+=\"; then\n90\t          # Final fallback: any non-assignment line referencing the var counts as \"used\".\n91\t          if ! grep -vE \"^[[:space:]]*${v}=\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null | grep -qE \"[\\\"]?\\\\\\$\\\\{?${v}\\\\}?[\\\"]?\"; then\n92\t            emit \"L-S13-1-ORPHAN-LOG-VAR\" \"$bn\" \"variable \\$${v} declared but never referenced after assignment\"\n93\t          fi\n94\t        fi\n95\t      fi\n96\t    done\n97\t  done\n98\tfi\n99\t\n100\t# === Check 3: D-IDENTITY S16 #10 — fabricated SUPERVISED-mode regression in LIVE config ===\n101\t# Per S15-close user correction (CHARTER-tier): full autonomous is the ONLY mode; \"SUPERVISED\"\n102\t# was a fabricated default-until-Track-7 framing that was never user-authorized. Scan LIVE\n103\t# config files; flag any `SUPERVISED|autonomous_mode:\\s*false|until Track 7` regression.\n104\t# Exempt historical session/checkpoint/decision/Q&A files (they record past state legitimately).\n105\tLIVE_TARGETS=(\n106\t  \"$PROJECT_DIR/.claude/settings.json\"\n107\t  \"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md\"\n108\t  \"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/project.md\"\n109\t  \"$PROJECT_DIR/CLAUDE.md\"\n110\t  \"$PROJECT_DIR/AGENT_OPERATING_MANUAL.md\"\n111\t)\n112\t# Live constitution + proposals (excluding archived/superseded versions).\n113\tif [ -d \"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/constitution\" ]; then\n114\t  while IFS= read -r -d '' p; do LIVE_TARGETS+=(\"$p\"); done < <(find \"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/constitution\" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)\n115\tfi\n116\tif [ -d \"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/proposals\" ]; then\n117\t  while IFS= read -r -d '' p; do LIVE_TARGETS+=(\"$p\"); done < <(find \"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/proposals\" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)\n118\tfi\n119\t\n120\tREGRESSION_PATTERN='SUPERVISED[[:space:]]*mode|autonomous_mode:[[:space:]]*false|until[[:space:]]+Track[[:space:]]+7|SUPERVISED-only'\n121\tfor t in \"${LIVE_TARGETS[@]}\"; do\n122\t  [ ! -f \"$t\" ] && continue\n123\t  rel=\"${t#$PROJECT_DIR/}\"\n124\t  # Scan; deny pattern matches but allow file to legitimately quote/document the rule itself.\n125\t  if grep -qE \"$REGRESSION_PATTERN\" \"$t\" 2>/dev/null; then\n126\t    # Allow if the line ALSO contains \"fabricated|deprecated|anti-pattern|never user-authorized\"\n127\t    # (i.e. file is documenting the prohibition, not violating it).\n128\t    HITS=\"$(grep -nE \"$REGRESSION_PATTERN\" \"$t\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n129\t    while IFS= read -r line; do\n130\t      [ -z \"$line\" ] && continue\n131\t      if printf '%s' \"$line\" | grep -qiE 'fabricated|deprecated|anti-pattern|never user-authorized|do NOT|MUST NOT|forbidden|not user-authorized'; then\n132\t        continue\n133\t      fi\n134\t      emit \"D-IDENTITY-AUTONOMOUS-REGRESSION\" \"$rel\" \"live-config line matches forbidden pattern: $(printf '%s' \"$line\" | cut -c1-100)\"\n135\t      break\n136\t    done <<< \"$HITS\"\n137\t  fi\n138\tdone\n139\t\n140\t# === Check 5: M-S51-1 grep-on-imagined-format anti-pattern (Pattern A) ===\n141\t# Origin: S51 T3.1 — promotion-cycle-trigger.sh greped literal `^\\*\\*Session N\\*\\*:` against\n142\t# real `## SXX —` header format → 0 matches → silent broken hook for ~12hr.\n143\t# Detection: literal \"Session N\" (capital-N placeholder; never a real header) appearing\n144\t# inside any grep/sed/awk argument. Also catches the variant with escaped asterisks.\n145\tif [ -d \"$HOOKS_DIR\" ]; then\n146\t  for f in \"$HOOKS_DIR\"/*.sh; do\n147\t    [ ! -f \"$f\" ] && continue\n148\t    bn=\"$(basename \"$f\")\"\n149\t    [ \"$bn\" = \"bash-hook-lint.sh\" ] && continue\n150\t    BAD_A=\"$(grep -nE \"(grep|sed|awk)[[:space:]].*Session N([^a-zA-Z0-9]|$)\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null | grep -vE \"^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*#\" || true)\"\n151\t    if [ -n \"$BAD_A\" ]; then\n152\t      emit \"M-S51-1-IMAGINED-FORMAT\" \"$bn\" \"literal 'Session N' placeholder in grep/sed/awk pattern — verify against real current-execution.md format (L-S51-1)\"\n153\t    fi\n154\t  done\n155\tfi\n156\t\n157\t# === Check 6: L-S48m-1 CLAUDE_SESSION_ID empty-on-Windows anti-pattern (Pattern B) ===\n158\t# Origin: S48m profile-template-auto-populate.sh — marker filename used $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID\n159\t# without :- fallback; on Windows the env var is empty → marker collides on every fire →\n160\t# silent skip after first fire. L-S48m-1 fix: use session-log basename instead.\n161\tif [ -d \"$HOOKS_DIR\" ]; then\n162\t  for f in \"$HOOKS_DIR\"/*.sh; do\n163\t    [ ! -f \"$f\" ] && continue\n164\t    bn=\"$(basename \"$f\")\"\n165\t    [ \"$bn\" = \"bash-hook-lint.sh\" ] && continue\n166\t    BAD_B=\"$(grep -nE \"[\\\"]?\\\\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+(-fired|-marker|-ran|-flag)-\\\\\\$\\\\{?CLAUDE_SESSION_ID\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null | grep -vE \"^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*#\" || true)\"\n167\t    if [ -n \"$BAD_B\" ]; then\n168\t      emit \"L-S48m-1-CLAUDE-SESSION-ID-MARKER\" \"$bn\" \"marker filename uses \\$CLAUDE_SESSION_ID (empty on Windows; silent skip — L-S48m-1)\"\n169\t    fi\n170\t  done\n171\tfi\n172\t\n173\t# === Check 7: L-S48d-1 pipefail+ERR-trap+bare-grep anti-pattern (Pattern C) — REFINED S58 ===\n174\t# Origin: S48d profile-template-auto-populate.sh — set -uo pipefail + trap 'exit 0' ERR\n175\t# + bare `grep -m1 ...` returning nonzero on no-match → ERR trap fires silently → script\n176\t# exits 0 with NO log line → invisible failure. Fix: wrap each grep with `|| true` or\n177\t# convert to `if grep ...; then ... fi` form.\n178\t#\n179\t# S54 refinement: caught command-sub + pipeline forms (was bare-line only).\n180\t#\n181\t# S58 refinement (closes KI-S54-1): replaces the 3-pass grep filter with an awk script\n182\t# that tracks pipefail-bracket state + multi-line `\\`-continuation joining + 4 NEW\n183\t# false-positive recognitions surfaced by S57 ratify-via-comment categorization sample:\n184\t#\n185\t#   NEW skip rules:\n186\t#     (1) Compound conditional `if X && grep`/`if X | grep`/`elif X && grep`/etc — line\n187\t#         starts with `if|while|until|elif` AND contains `grep` (cond exit consumed by `if`)\n188\t#     (2) Alt-guard `|| echo NN`/`|| echo \"\"`/`|| echo` end-of-pipeline (substitute\n189\t#         non-zero with echo output → command-sub/pipeline returns 0 → ERR trap exempt)\n190\t#     (3) Alt-guard `|| exit N`/`|| return N` (explicit exit handling)\n191\t#     (4) Pipefail-bracket `set +o pipefail; grep; set -o pipefail` (pipefail temporarily\n192\t#         disabled so grep no-match is safe; double-defense pattern)\n193\t#\n194\t# Plus existing skip rules (preserved):\n195\t#   - Comment lines (`^NN:#`)\n196\t#   - Direct conditional `if grep`/`while grep`/`until grep`/`elif grep`\n197\t#   - Already-guarded `|| true`/`|| :`\n198\t#\n199\t# Multi-line `\\`-continuation: physical lines ending with `\\` are joined with the next\n200\t# physical line before pattern testing (catches drift-signals-D1-D9.sh:178-180 form\n201\t# where alt-guard `|| echo 0` is on the LAST continuation line of a 3-line pipeline).\n202\t#\n203\t# Initial pipefail state: OFF (matches bash default; flips ON when first\n204\t# `set -[a-zA-Z]*o pipefail` seen; flips OFF when `set +o pipefail` seen).\n205\tif [ -d \"$HOOKS_DIR\" ]; then\n206\t  for f in \"$HOOKS_DIR\"/*.sh; do\n207\t    [ ! -f \"$f\" ] && continue\n208\t    bn=\"$(basename \"$f\")\"\n209\t    [ \"$bn\" = \"bash-hook-lint.sh\" ] && continue\n210\t    HAS_PIPEFAIL=\"$(grep -cE 'set [^#]*pipefail' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\"\n211\t    HAS_ERR_TRAP=\"$(grep -cE 'trap[[:space:]]+[^#]*ERR' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\"\n212\t    if [ \"$HAS_PIPEFAIL\" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && [ \"$HAS_ERR_TRAP\" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then\n213\t      VIOLATION_LINE=\"$(awk '\n214\tBEGIN { pipefail_off = 1; carry = \"\" }\n215\t{\n216\t  line = $0\n217\t  # Match physical line ending with literal `\\` (backslash continuation).\n218\t  # /\\\\$/ in awk source = regex `\\\\` (literal backslash) + `$` (EOL anchor).\n219\t  # Confirmed empirically: `awk '/\\\\$/'` matches lines ending with literal `\\`.\n220\t  if (line ~ /\\\\$/) {\n221\t    sub(/\\\\$/, \"\", line)\n222\t    carry = (carry == \"\" ? line : carry \" \" line)\n223\t    next\n224\t  }\n225\t  full = (carry == \"\" ? line : carry \" \" line)\n226\t  carry = \"\"\n227\t\n228\t  if (full ~ /^[[:space:]]*set[[:space:]]+\\+o[[:space:]]+pipefail/) {\n229\t    pipefail_off = 1\n230\t    next\n231\t  }\n232\t  if (full ~ /^[[:space:]]*set[[:space:]]+-[a-zA-Z]*o[[:space:]]+pipefail/) {\n233\t    pipefail_off = 0\n234\t    next\n235\t  }\n236\t  if (pipefail_off) next\n237\t  if (full ~ /^[[:space:]]*#/) next\n238\t  if (full ~ /grep[[:space:]]/) {\n239\t    if (full ~ /^[[:space:]]*(if|while|until|elif)[[:space:]]/) next\n240\t    if (full ~ /grep[[:space:]].*[[:space:]](&&|\\|\\|)[[:space:]]/) next\n241\t    print NR \":\" full\n242\t    exit\n243\t  }\n244\t}\n245\t' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n246\t      if [ -n \"$VIOLATION_LINE\" ]; then\n247\t        emit \"L-S48d-1-PIPEFAIL-BARE-GREP\" \"$bn\" \"pipefail + ERR trap + grep without guard — silent fail risk (L-S48d-1; refined S58 to recognize compound-if + alt-guard echo/exit/return + pipefail-bracket + multi-line continuation)\"\n248\t      fi\n249\t    fi\n250\t  done\n251\tfi\n252\t\n253\t# === Check 8: L-S53-2 unanchored positional-marker grep (NEW Pattern D) — S54 ===\n254\t# Origin: S53 M-S53-2 — `session-export-raw.sh` Method 1 grep `'S[0-9]+[[:space:]]+NEXT'`\n255\t# without ^ anchor matched archive prose mid-line \"S38/S42 NEXT branching gate\" →\n256\t# returned false-positive 42 every export, silently corrupted ALL raw-session filenames.\n257\t# Detection: 2-pass — (a) find grep lines whose pattern contains routing-marker regex\n258\t# tokens (S[0-9]+, Track [0-9]+, Session N, Session [0-9]+, ## S[0-9]+); (b) exclude\n259\t# lines where the pattern body starts with `^` anchor (whitelist).\n260\tif [ -d \"$HOOKS_DIR\" ]; then\n261\t  for f in \"$HOOKS_DIR\"/*.sh; do\n262\t    [ ! -f \"$f\" ] && continue\n263\t    bn=\"$(basename \"$f\")\"\n264\t    [ \"$bn\" = \"bash-hook-lint.sh\" ] && continue\n265\t    BAD_D=\"$(grep -nE \"grep[[:space:]]+(-[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*[[:space:]]+)*['\\\"][^'\\\"]*(S\\[0-9\\]\\+|Track[[:space:]]+\\[0-9|Session[[:space:]]+(N|\\[0-9)|## S\\[0-9)\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null \\\n266\t      | grep -vE \"grep[[:space:]]+(-[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*[[:space:]]+)*['\\\"]\\^\" \\\n267\t      | grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*#' \\\n268\t      || true)\"\n269\t    if [ -n \"$BAD_D\" ]; then\n270\t      emit \"L-S53-2-UNANCHORED-POSITIONAL-GREP\" \"$bn\" \"grep with routing-marker pattern (S<N>/Track/Session/## S<N>) lacks '^' anchor — mid-line false-positive risk (L-S53-2)\"\n271\t    fi\n272\t  done\n273\tfi\n274\t\n275\t# === Check 9: L-S68-2 family — find/ls on possibly-missing path under pipefail+ERR-trap (NEW S80) ===\n276\t# Origin: 4 instances across S68/S75/S76/S78. Family precondition: file has BOTH `set -*o pipefail`\n277\t# AND `trap ... ERR`. In that mode, `find $missing -mtime`/`ls $dir/*.glob` returns rc=1 silently\n278\t# if path missing or glob has no match → ERR trap fires → script silent-exits 0 BEFORE work runs.\n279\t#\n280\t# Variants (combined detector):\n281\t#   (a) Single-path `find $path -...` (literal var; no glob) — S68+S75\n282\t#   (b) `ls $dir/*.glob` (no-match returns rc=1 under pipefail) — S76\n283\t#   (c) Multi-path `find $a $b $c -...` (rc=1 if ANY arg missing) — S78\n284\t#\n285\t# Skip rules (all three variants):\n286\t#   - Comment lines (^NN: # )\n287\t#   - Line starts with `if|while|until|elif`\n288\t#   - Alt-guarded with `|| true|:|return|exit|echo`\n289\t#   - Errors silenced with `2>/dev/null`\n290\t#   - Pipefail bracket disabled (`set +o pipefail` in effect)\n291\t#   - File-test guard `[ -d ... ]` or `[ -f ... ]` on SAME line (catches `[ -d $X ] && find $X`)\n292\t#   - Variant (b) only: `shopt -s nullglob` set anywhere above (glob no-match → empty list, no rc=1)\n293\t#\n294\t# Multi-line `\\`-continuation: physical lines joined with carry before pattern-matching, so multi-arg\n295\t# find spread across multiple lines is tested as one logical line (catches `2>/dev/null` on tail).\n296\tif [ -d \"$HOOKS_DIR\" ]; then\n297\t  for f in \"$HOOKS_DIR\"/*.sh; do\n298\t    [ ! -f \"$f\" ] && continue\n299\t    bn=\"$(basename \"$f\")\"\n300\t    [ \"$bn\" = \"bash-hook-lint.sh\" ] && continue\n301\t    HAS_PIPEFAIL=\"$(grep -cE 'set [^#]*pipefail' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\"\n302\t    HAS_ERR_TRAP=\"$(grep -cE 'trap[[:space:]]+[^#]*ERR' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\"\n303\t    if [ \"$HAS_PIPEFAIL\" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && [ \"$HAS_ERR_TRAP\" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then\n304\t      # Clean 0/1 (avoids \"0\\n0\" from `grep -c` exit-1 + `|| echo 0` race that breaks awk's numeric coercion)\n305\t      if grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*shopt[[:space:]]+-s[[:space:]]+nullglob' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null; then HAS_NULLGLOB=1; else HAS_NULLGLOB=0; fi\n306\t      VIOLATION_LINE_E=\"$(awk -v has_nullglob=\"$HAS_NULLGLOB\" '\n307\tBEGIN { pipefail_off = 1; carry = \"\" }\n308\t{\n309\t  line = $0\n310\t  # Match physical line ending with literal `\\` (backslash continuation).\n311\t  # /\\\\$/ in awk source = regex `\\\\` (literal backslash) + `$` (EOL anchor).\n312\t  # Confirmed empirically: `awk '/\\\\$/'` matches lines ending with literal `\\`.\n313\t  if (line ~ /\\\\$/) {\n314\t    sub(/\\\\$/, \"\", line)\n315\t    carry = (carry == \"\" ? line : carry \" \" line)\n316\t    next\n317\t  }\n318\t  full = (carry == \"\" ? line : carry \" \" line)\n319\t  carry = \"\"\n320\t\n321\t  if (full ~ /^[[:space:]]*set[[:space:]]+\\+o[[:space:]]+pipefail/) { pipefail_off = 1; next }\n322\t  if (full ~ /^[[:space:]]*set[[:space:]]+-[a-zA-Z]*o[[:space:]]+pipefail/) { pipefail_off = 0; next }\n323\t  if (pipefail_off) next\n324\t  if (full ~ /^[[:space:]]*#/) next\n325\t\n326\t  body = full\n327\t  sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, \"\", body)\n328\t\n329\t  # Skip lines starting with conditional keywords\n330\t  if (body ~ /^(if|while|until|elif)[[:space:]]/) next\n331\t\n332\t  # Skip alt-guarded with || true|:|return|exit|echo\n333\t  if (full ~ /\\|\\|[[:space:]]+(true|:|return|exit|echo)/) next\n334\t\n335\t  # Skip if errors silenced\n336\t  if (full ~ /2>\\/dev\\/null/) next\n337\t\n338\t  # Skip if same-line file-test guard (catches `[ -d $X ] && find $X`)\n339\t  if (full ~ /\\[[[:space:]]+-[df][[:space:]]+/) next\n340\t\n341\t  # === Variant (a) + (c): find <var/literal>... ===\n342\t  # Match `find` token followed by quoted/unquoted $var arg.\n343\t  if (body ~ /(^|[[:space:]`(|&;])find[[:space:]]+[\"]?\\$/) {\n344\t    print NR \":(find-variant) \" full\n345\t    exit\n346\t  }\n347\t\n348\t  # === Variant (b): ls $dir/*.glob ===\n349\t  # Match `ls` token followed by arg(s) containing a `$var` AND a glob `*` somewhere after.\n350\t  # Permissive on intermediate chars (handles `ls \"$DIR\"/*.md`, `ls ${X}/*.tsv`, etc.).\n351\t  # Skip if shopt -s nullglob set in file (glob no-match → empty list, no rc=1).\n352\t  if (has_nullglob == 0 && body ~ /(^|[[:space:]`(|&;])ls[[:space:]]+[^|&;]*\\$[^|&;]*\\*/) {\n353\t    print NR \":(ls-glob-variant) \" full\n354\t    exit\n355\t  }\n356\t}\n357\t' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n358\t      if [ -n \"$VIOLATION_LINE_E\" ]; {"parentUuid":"2f9e7bc7-8343-4a16-962d-00635f08854e","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"99bcfc61-6b7e-4692-9e26-f8efdc04f543","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01JkoadtFrDko62AFvn3MUtv","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\scripts\\hooks\\drift-signals-D1-D9.sh has been updated successfully."}]},"uuid":"ded56a1d-3da2-4ecf-bc9a-677abd27ff75","timestamp":"2026-05-06T07:42:43.829Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\scripts\\hooks\\drift-signals-D1-D9.sh","oldString":"  HIGH_COUNT=\"$(grep -c \"severity=HIGH\" \"$LOG\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)\"","newString":"  HIGH_COUNT=\"$(grep -c \"severity=HIGH\" \"$LOG\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"","originalFile":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# drift-signals-D1-D9.sh — composite drift detector running 9 grep-based signals.\n# D1 = LOC ceiling overrun (PRIMARY per Q-A2 answer 2026-04-29: highest empirical firing\n# rate at S2). D2-D8 = secondary checks. D9 = runtime-path-leak into write-only\n# learning-data/(events|archive)/ tree (Track 5.5d.1 D-5 deliverable per D-005).\n# Append violations to .drift-signals.log.\n# Decision 002 § Track 5 REV-2 § B + Decision 005 § 5.5d.1.\nset -uo pipefail\ntrap 'exit 0' ERR\n\n# === L-S48d-1 lint flag — S57 retrofit (1 real fix + KI-S54-1 ratify) ===\n# bash-hook-lint Check 7 flags this file. Categorization:\n#   FIXED S57: D4-loop bare-grep `REFS=\"$(grep -oE ... | sort -u | head -5)\"`\n#     was unguarded — no-match returned 1 → pipefail propagated → ERR-trap\n#     `exit 0` silently aborted spec scanning. Added `|| true` end-of-pipeline.\n#     REAL bug, not alt-guard form (only one in this file).\n#   Many `if grep -qE ...; then` and `if ! grep -qiE ...; then` forms — exit\n#     consumed by `if` → ERR-trap exempt per bash spec ✓\n#   Many `VAR=\"$(grep ... | wc -l | tr -d '...' || echo 0)\"` — alt-guard\n#     `|| echo 0` end-of-pipeline ✓ (KI-S54-1 recognition)\n#   `if [ X = \"1\" ] && grep -q ...; then` (line ~202) — `&&`-chain in `if` ✓\n# Per-file Check 7 design keeps flag (alt-guards not normalized to `|| true`).\n# Lint refinement deferred per KI-S54-1.\n\nPROJECT_DIR=\"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}\"\nmkdir -p \"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory\"\nLOG=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/.drift-signals.log\"\nHOOK_LOG=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/.session-hooks.log\"\nTS=\"$(date -Iseconds)\"\n\nVIOLATIONS=0\n\nemit() {\n  local signal=\"$1\" severity=\"$2\" detail=\"$3\"\n  printf '[%s] %s severity=%s %s\\n' \"$TS\" \"$signal\" \"$severity\" \"$detail\" >> \"$LOG\"\n  VIOLATIONS=$(( VIOLATIONS + 1 ))\n}\n\n# === D1: LOC ceiling overrun (PRIMARY) — agents 200, skills 150, commands 120 ===\ncheck_loc() {\n  local file=\"$1\" ceiling=\"$2\" archetype=\"$3\"\n  [ ! -f \"$file\" ] && return\n  local lines\n  lines=\"$(wc -l < \"$file\" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')\"\n  [[ \"$lines\" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return\n  local overrun_pct=$(( (lines - ceiling) * 100 / ceiling ))\n  if [ \"$lines\" -gt \"$ceiling\" ]; then\n    if [ \"$overrun_pct\" -ge 20 ]; then\n      emit \"D1-LOC-CEILING\" \"HIGH\" \"file=$file archetype=$archetype lines=$lines ceiling=$ceiling overrun_pct=$overrun_pct\"\n    else\n      emit \"D1-LOC-CEILING\" \"MEDIUM\" \"file=$file archetype=$archetype lines=$lines ceiling=$ceiling overrun_pct=$overrun_pct\"\n    fi\n  fi\n}\n\nfor f in \"$PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/agents/*.md; do\n  check_loc \"$f\" 200 \"agent\"\ndone\nfor f in \"$PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do\n  check_loc \"$f\" 150 \"skill\"\ndone\nfor f in \"$PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/commands/*.md; do\n  check_loc \"$f\" 120 \"command\"\ndone\n\n# === D2: Self-attestation contradicting actual (text claims X LOC but file is Y) ===\n# Heuristic grep: session logs claiming \"within target\" or \"<150 LOC\" without wc -l command nearby.\nSESSION_LOGS=\"$(find \"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory/sessions\" -name '*.md' -mmin -1440 2>/dev/null || true)\"\nfor s in $SESSION_LOGS; do\n  [ ! -f \"$s\" ] && continue\n  if grep -qE '(LOC|line count|bodies are.*LOC|within target)' \"$s\" 2>/dev/null; then\n    if ! grep -qE 'wc -l' \"$s\" 2>/dev/null; then\n      emit \"D2-SELF-ATTEST\" \"MEDIUM\" \"file=$s claim=LOC-within-target without-wc-l-verification\"\n    fi\n  fi\ndone\n\n# === D3: Charter-tier item bundled with sub-charter-tier (silent absorption risk) ===\nQA_BUNDLES=\"$(find \"$PROJECT_DIR/human-workspace/q-and-a/pending\" \\\n                   \"$PROJECT_DIR/human-workspace/q-and-a/answered\" \\\n              -name '*.md' -mmin -1440 2>/dev/null || true)\"\nfor b in $QA_BUNDLES; do\n  [ ! S74 fix per L-S74-1 — was latent S73 finding.\nRAW_PATH=$(grep -oE '(agent-workspace/)?session-plans/pending/[0-9-]+[^ )\"`]+\\.md' \"$EXEC_FILE\" | head -1 || true)\n[ -z \"$RAW_PATH\" ] && exit 0\n# Normalize: ensure agent-workspace/ prefix (production layout).\ncase \"$RAW_PATH\" in\n  agent-workspace/*) ACTIVE_PLAN=\"$RAW_PATH\" ;;\n  *) ACTIVE_PLAN=\"agent-workspace/$RAW_PATH\" ;;\nesac\n[ ! -f \"$PROJECT_DIR/$ACTIVE_PLAN\" ] && exit 0\n\n# Whitelist of vendor libraries we care about (extend as project grows).\nVENDOR_LIBS=\"vnstock yfinance httpx anthropic openai duckdb pgvector\"\n\nVIOLATIONS=0\nfor LIB in $VENDOR_LIBS; do\n  if grep -qE \"(import $LIB|from $LIB|$LIB\\.)\" \"$PROJECT_DIR/$ACTIVE_PLAN\"; then\n    # Probe library importability + version.\n    PROBE=$(python -c \"\nimport importlib, sys\ntry:\n    m = importlib.import_module('$LIB')\n    v = getattr(m, '__version__', 'unknown')\n    print(f'OK $LIB v={v}')\nexcept Exception as e:\n    print(f'FAIL $LIB err={e}')\n    sys.exit(1)\n\" 2>&1) || true\n    if echo \"$PROBE\" | grep -q '^FAIL';
